title: A hash table with open addressing
description:
Build `IdTable`, a hash table mapping `std::uint32_t` ids to `int` values, using **open addressing with linear probing**.

The table has a fixed number of slots, given to the constructor. Each slot is either empty or holds one key and its value.

- The home slot of a key is `hash(key) % slotCount`, where `hash` is the function given below.
- `insert(key, value)`: start at the home slot and move one slot at a time (wrapping round to 0 after the last slot) until you find either the same key, whose value you then replace, or an empty slot, where you put the new entry. Return `true`. If every slot is full of other keys, return `false`.
- `find(key)`: probe the same way. Return the value if you meet the key; return `std::nullopt` when you reach an empty slot or have looked at every slot.
- `size()`: how many keys are stored.

There is no removing in this task (removal in open addressing needs special "deleted" markers).
hints: `std::optional<T>` (from `<optional>`) holds either a `T` or nothing. `return value;` gives back a filled one and `return std::nullopt;` an empty one. A caller tests it with `if (result)` (or `result.has_value()`) and reads the value inside with `*result`.
Both `insert` and `find` use the same loop: start at `hash(key) % n`, look at up to `n` slots, and step with `i = (i + 1) % n`.
In `insert`, an empty slot means "put it here" and the same key means "replace". In `find`, an empty slot means "it is not in the table": if it were, it would have been placed here or earlier.
Guard against a table with 0 slots before using `% n`.
